implementerProof.how: Both failures of the round before are answered. The pull request is MERGEABLE again and GitHub builds it. The probe's A8 pair, which was a coin flip on four runs of mine, now takes the project's twenty commonest words and is green with a clear margin on my run too: 20.764ms before against 19.712ms after, -5.1%. Everything the implementer reports was re-run at this head and holds: the census on a production-shaped main-schema database, all thirteen protocol 1 pairs, protocol 2's two sides, A9's six routes, the reads over HTTP and the live refresh. The one thing red is a lane this change does not own (below).

failures.criterion: CI green at the head, which the merge gate needs.
failures.evidence: dispatch-memory fails at the code head c635577e (job 125108252089): 'a cold one-word edit of a two-column table held 281 MiB above idle, want at most 256 MiB', in TestAColdEditOfTheHeaviestDocumentsStaysWithinTheMemoryBound, a test of main's own cold-edit memory bound (#1891). It is main's, not this change's: the same lane is green at four earlier heads of this branch (a50b56b9, b858997d, 8afd81a7, c0760a8d), and it fails on main itself at b552205c8 - the commit this round's forward merge brought in - with 301 MiB, twenty above what this head reads. So main's own code is over the bound at that commit while this head is nearer to it, and main's later commit 11ca14268 reads the lane green, which says the measurement sits on the bound rather than far past it. The remedy is not in this change: re-run the lane, and if it repeats, it waits on main's fix and another forward merge. Everything else at the head is green - 27 pass, one skipped, only the ci-ok aggregator still queued.

proof.criterion: A9, the write bound: the median of 50 requests to each of the six write routes rises by no more than 10%.
proof.surface: The base server, built from the merge's main parent, on the main-schema copy, and this head's server on the head copy, each driven by the committed harness, with the order of the two sides reversed in every other round as the implementer's note asks, since both databases live on one Postgres.

proof.observed: Every route inside the bound, and four of the six faster. Against the highest base run: comments 23.7 ms -> +2.9%, +2.8%, +6.2%; asks 5044.6 ms -> -0.1%, -0.1%, -0.1%; messages 24.6 ms -> -16.9%, -16.8%, -16.9%; the small upload 260.0 ms -> -73.5%, -75.5%, -75.5%; the large upload 741.7 ms -> -39.8%, -36.7%, -39.9%; the title edit 38.3 ms -> -8.9%, -12.7%, -12.5%.

One absolute to read with care, which the bound is unaffected by: the ask route costs about 5.04 s on both sides, because the measured issue has taken 50 asks a run from every A9 round this phase and the implementer's, and the route's cost grows with the issue's asks. Both sides carry the same history, so the ratio stands; the absolute is the fixture's.
